# bitbucket_project_branching_model (Resource)

Configures the default development/production branch settings inherited by every repository in a Bitbucket Cloud project. There is exactly one of these per project; Bitbucket has no delete endpoint for it, so destroying this resource only removes it from state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "bitbucket_project_branching_model" "platform" {
  project_key                = bitbucket_project.platform.key
  development_use_mainbranch = true
  production_enabled         = true
  production_branch          = "production"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_key` (String) Key of the project to configure.

### Optional

- `development_branch` (String) Name of the development branch. Ignored if development_use_mainbranch is true.
- `development_use_mainbranch` (Boolean) Use each repository's main branch as the development branch. Defaults to true.
- `production_branch` (String) Name of the production branch. Ignored if production_use_mainbranch is true.
- `production_enabled` (Boolean) Whether a production branch is configured. Defaults to false.
- `production_use_mainbranch` (Boolean) Use each repository's main branch as the production branch. Defaults to false.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier, formatted as "workspace/project_key".

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import bitbucket_project_branching_model.platform PLAT
```
